text:
John initially has 13 Lego sets. He sells some of them at $15 each. He buys 8 video games at $20 each, spending \(8 \times 20 = \$160\), and has $5 left. So the total money he had from selling Lego sets is \(160 + 5 = \$165\). Since each set sells for $15, the number of sets he sold is \(165 \div 15 = 11\). Therefore, the number of Lego sets he still has is \(13 - 11 = 2\).

Answer: 2
reasoning:
We are given: "John plans to sell all his toys and use the money to buy video games. He has 13 lego sets and he sells them for $15 each. He ends up buying 8 video games for $20 each and has $5 left. How many lego sets does he still have?"

He ends up buying 8 video games for $20 each and has $5 left. How many lego sets does he still have?"

It says "He has 13 lego sets and he sells them for $15 each." It might mean he sells some of them, not all? But it says "plans to sell all his toys". Then "He ends up buying 8 video games... and has $5 left." So he sold some number of lego sets, got money, bought 8 video games for $20 each (total $160), and had $5 left, so he had $165 total from selling. If each lego set is $15, then number of lego sets sold = 165 / 15 = 11. He originally had 13 lego sets. So he still has 13 - 11 = 2 lego sets. The phrase "plans to sell all his toys" might be a bit of misdirection, or it means that was his plan, but he only needed to sell some to get the video games and have $5 left, so he didn't sell all. The question asks how many he still has, implying he didn't sell all.

Thus answer: 2.
